# peterbono/ai-design-system-demo design system

> Tokens, components and usage guidance of the design system in github.com/peterbono/ai-design-system-demo, read at fb8c259 on main (2026-10-24). Published by Bridge for AI agents and people.

- Source: https://github.com/peterbono/ai-design-system-demo/tree/fb8c259b311182cac837c04da6d60259ba8fe8da
- Every file Bridge read, as JSON: snapshot.json, next to this file on the bridge-data branch.
- Themes: light, dark. Brands: bridge, ocean. Densities: comfortable, compact.

## Tokens

386 tokens (brand, semantic, density and component tiers) on top of 254 primitives. Use the semantic tokens in product code, never the primitives. Values are for the default brand (bridge).

- `color.bg.default` (`--color-bg-default`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #0b1825. Page canvas. White in bridge, so content sits on paper; ocean keeps a tinted canvas.
- `color.bg.subtle` (`--color-bg-subtle`, semantic color): light #edeff2, dark #15202b. Recessed areas: table headers, code blocks, footers.
- `color.bg.muted` (`--color-bg-muted`, semantic color): light #e3e8ee, dark #323e4c. Tracks, skeletons, neutral fills.
- `color.bg.zone` (`--color-bg-zone`, semantic color): light #cfe8ff, dark #00274b. Large flat color blocks that open a space: the home hero, section page headers, the Studio greeting, onboarding. Never behind dense UI.
- `color.surface.default` (`--color-surface-default`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #15202b. Panels, cards, inputs.
- `color.surface.raised` (`--color-surface-raised`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #323e4c. Floating layers: popovers, menus, dialogs, toasts.
- `color.surface.hover` (`--color-surface-hover`, semantic color): light #edeff2, dark #323e4c. Hover fill for rows, menu items, ghost controls.
- `color.surface.hover-raised` (`--color-surface-hover-raised`, semantic color): light #edeff2, dark #495562. Hover fill inside a raised surface.
- `color.surface.pressed` (`--color-surface-pressed`, semantic color): light #e3e8ee, dark #495562. Pressed fill.
- `color.surface.selected` (`--color-surface-selected`, semantic color): light #f1f8ff, dark #001732. Selected rows and items. Paired with a checked control or a mark, never alone.
- `color.surface.inverse` (`--color-surface-inverse`, semantic color): light #15202b, dark #edeff2. Tooltips and inverse chips.
- `color.surface.strong` (`--color-surface-strong`, semantic color): light #0b4a8b, dark #0b4a8b. Deep Harbor in both themes, for a mode the whole page is in (Banner appearance strong). Text on it: text.on-solid. Dark keeps it dark, so it never reads as the Harbor zone or the light primary action of the dark theme.
- `color.text.default` (`--color-text-default`, semantic color): light #15202b, dark #f5f7f9
- `color.text.muted` (`--color-text-muted`, semantic color): light #5b6672, dark #a0aab5. Secondary text. 4.5:1 on every background.
- `color.text.disabled` (`--color-text-disabled`, semantic color): light #a0aab5, dark #5b6672. Disabled text. Exempt from contrast minimums; never the only cue.
- `color.text.inverse` (`--color-text-inverse`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #0b1825. Text on surface.inverse.
- `color.text.on-solid` (`--color-text-on-solid`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #ffffff. Text and icons on feedback and danger solids.
- `color.text.link` (`--color-text-link`, semantic color): light #0b4a8b, dark #aad2fe
- `color.text.link-hover` (`--color-text-link-hover`, semantic color): light #043e70, dark #cfe8ff
- `color.text.signal` (`--color-text-signal`, semantic color): light #0b4a8b, dark #aad2fe. Signal-colored text (match highlights, current step).
- `color.border.default` (`--color-border-default`, semantic color): light #e3e8ee, dark #323e4c. Hairlines: card edges, dividers. Decorative, no contrast minimum.
- `color.border.subtle` (`--color-border-subtle`, semantic color): light #edeff2, dark #15202b. Row separators inside tables and lists.
- `color.border.strong` (`--color-border-strong`, semantic color): light #808a96, dark #808a96. Edges that identify a control (inputs, checkboxes, switches). 3:1 against surfaces (WCAG 1.4.11).
- `color.border.emphasis` (`--color-border-emphasis`, semantic color): light #c6cfd9, dark #495562. A hairline that must read before the default one: hovered cards, group dividers, dashed placeholders. Decorative, no contrast minimum.
- `color.border.hover` (`--color-border-hover`, semantic color): light #5b6672, dark #a0aab5. Control edge on hover.
- `color.action.primary.bg` (`--color-action-primary-bg`, semantic color): light #0b4a8b, dark #aad2fe. Primary action fill (steel ink in the bridge brand).
- `color.action.primary.bg-hover` (`--color-action-primary-bg-hover`, semantic color): light #043e70, dark #cfe8ff
- `color.action.primary.bg-active` (`--color-action-primary-bg-active`, semantic color): light #00274b, dark #e4f1fe

- `color.control.bg` (`--color-control-bg`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #15202b. Unchecked checkbox, radio, input fill.
- `color.control.checked.bg` (`--color-control-checked-bg`, semantic color): light #0b4a8b, dark #aad2fe. Checked checkbox, radio, switch track. Selection is ink.
- `color.control.checked.bg-hover` (`--color-control-checked-bg-hover`, semantic color): light #043e70, dark #cfe8ff
- `color.control.checked.fg` (`--color-control-checked-fg`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #001732. Check mark, radio dot, switch thumb when checked.
- `color.control.track` (`--color-control-track`, semantic color): light #808a96, dark #808a96. Unchecked switch track and slider rail edge. 3:1 against surfaces.
- `color.control.thumb` (`--color-control-thumb`, semantic color): light #ffffff, dark #f5f7f9
- `color.signal.default` (`--color-signal-default`, semantic color): light #1b6eb9, dark #6eaef2. The signal: active indicators, progress, slider range.
- `color.signal.subtle` (`--color-signal-subtle`, semantic color): light #e4f1fe, dark #00274b. Soft signal fill: highlighted search matches.

## Components

### Icon

Draws a Lucide icon at a token size with the system stroke width, in the color of the text around it. Decorative by default: pass a label only when the icon carries meaning on its own.

- Family: Foundations
- Tokens: icon.size.lg, icon.size.md, icon.size.sm, icon.size.xs, icon.stroke
- Use it for:
  - Next to a label, to help people scan: a menu item, a tab, a status line, a table cell.
  - Inside your own controls, at size sm (16), the size the system uses in controls.
  - In navigation at size md (20), so the side nav reads at a glance.
  - Any Lucide glyph: pass the component itself, for example icon={GitBranch} imported from lucide-react.
- Not for:
  - As the only content of a button: use IconButton, which requires a label and sizes the hit area.
  - Inside Button or Badge when they place the icon for you: Button takes iconStart and iconEnd, Badge takes icon.
  - Emoji or Unicode glyphs standing in for icons: the system uses one family, Lucide.
  - Illustrations or logos: Icon draws 24px grid line icons only.
- Accessibility:
  - Without label, the icon gets aria-hidden="true": screen readers skip it and read the text next to it.
  - With label, it gets role="img" and aria-label, so it is announced as an image with that name.
  - focusable="false" keeps the SVG out of the tab order. Make the parent control focusable, never the icon.
  - The icon inherits the text color, so it gets the same contrast as the label it sits next to.
- Do: Pair the icon with text. The word carries the meaning and the icon helps people find it. The icon stays hidden from screen readers, so the label is read once.
- Do: Pick the size from the token scale. xs 12, sm 16, md 20, lg 24. The stroke stays at icon.stroke on every size, so icons keep the weight of the text.
- Do: Give a label when the icon stands alone and means something. With label, Icon becomes role="img" with that accessible name. Say what it means ("Merged"), not what it shows ("Purple circle").
- Don't: Set a color or a size by hand. Icon inherits currentColor and takes its size from the icon size tokens. A hard-coded width or color drifts from the theme and the density.
- Don't: Rely on the icon alone to say a status. Color and shape are not enough for everyone. Put the status in words next to it, or use Badge.

### VisuallyHidden

Text for assistive technology only: screen readers read it, the screen does not show it. Use it to give a control or a symbol the words sighted users get from the layout.

- Family: Foundations
- Tokens: border.width.1
- Use it for:
  - A control whose visible content is not enough on its own, like a checkbox in a table row: "Select Button".
  - Extra context a sighted user gets from the layout, like " (opens in a new tab)" after an external link.
  - A label for a loading region while Skeleton placeholders are shown, like "Loading tokens".
- Not for:
  - Hiding content from everyone: use the hidden attribute or do not render it.
  - Naming an icon-only button: IconButton takes a label prop for that.
  - Long text or anything interactive: it is a span clipped to one pixel, so a link or button inside it would take focus while staying invisible.
- Accessibility:
  - Renders a span that stays in the accessibility tree: screen readers read its text in place.
  - Clipped to one pixel with clip-path and overflow hidden, positioned absolutely, so it takes no room in the layout.
  - white-space: nowrap keeps the words from being read one per line by some screen readers.
  - Accepts every native span attribute and spreads them, so an id for aria-describedby works.
- Do: Add the words the layout implies. Link with external does it for you: it adds a VisuallyHidden " (opens in a new tab)" after the label.
- Do: Keep it short and specific. Name the thing the control acts on: "Select Button" in a row, "Select all tokens" in the header.
- Don't: Repeat what is already visible. If the visible label says it, screen readers read it twice.
- Don't: Use it to hide content you want to remove. Screen reader users still hear it. Remove the content, or use the hidden attribute.

### Button

Triggers an action on the current screen: save, publish, approve, open a dialog. If it takes the user somewhere else, it is a Link, not a Button.

- Family: Actions
- Tokens: border-width.default, border-width.strong, button.danger.bg, button.danger.bg-active, button.danger.bg-hover, button.danger.text, button.font-weight, button.ghost.bg-active, button.ghost.bg-hover, button.ghost.text, button.primary.bg, button.primary.bg-active, button.primary.bg-hover, button.primary.text, button.radius, button.secondary.bg, button.secondary.bg-active, button.secondary.bg-hover, button.secondary.border, button.secondary.text, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.control.checked.bg, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.surface.default, color.surface.hover, color.surface.pressed, color.surface.selected, color.text.default, color.text.link, color.text.link-hover, control.gap, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.lg, control.padding-x.md, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, ...
- Use it for:
  - The user commits an action on this screen: Publish, Approve, Create token, Open pull request.
  - Primary: the one action you most want the user to take in this view. One per form, dialog or page section.
  - Secondary: the alternatives next to the primary, like Save as draft or Request changes.
  - Ghost: low-emphasis actions repeated in lists, tables or toolbars (Edit, View diff), where filled buttons would fight for attention.
  - Danger: destructive actions (Delete, Revoke access). Usually inside a confirmation dialog.
  - Pressed: a toggle that stays on, like Compare or Show what changed in a toolbar. Set pressed to true or false; the selected look and aria-pressed follow it.
  - Link: an action on this screen inside a sentence, like "Show only these" after a count. It looks like a link and stays a button.
  - Inverse: the action on a strong surface (Deep Harbor, the inverse terminal bars), where secondary would disappear.
  - Size sm in dense rows and toolbars, md everywhere else, lg only for a single call to action on an empty or onboarding screen. Heights follow the density setting.
- Not for:
  - Going to another page or URL: use Link. Links and buttons are announced differently and users expect Cmd+click to open links in a new tab.
  - Navigation with variant link: a link-looking button still does not go anywhere. Use Link to go to another page.
  - Turning a setting on or off in a form: use Switch or Checkbox. A pressed Button is for toolbar toggles that change the view.
  - Picking one of several views: use Tabs or an attached ButtonGroup.
  - More than three actions in one row: keep the main ones and move the rest to a Menu behind an IconButton.
- Accessibility:
  - Native button through Base UI: Enter and Space activate it, it is in the tab order, no extra ARIA needed.
  - The focus ring (focus.ring.color, 2px, offset 2px) shows on keyboard focus only, never on mouse click.
  - Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, ignores clicks, and keeps the button focusable so keyboard users keep their place.
  - Disabled removes the button from the tab order and explains nothing. Prefer an enabled button plus a message saying what is missing.
  - pressed sets aria-pressed, so screen readers announce a toggle button and its state. Leave it unset on plain buttons: aria-pressed false still announces a toggle.
  - Variant link keeps the native button: Enter and Space work, it is announced as a button, and the focus ring is the DS ring.
  - With render={<a href />} the element stays a link (role link), which is right for navigation styled as a button.
  - Heights are 32/40/48px comfortable and 28/32/40px compact: all above the WCAG 2.2 minimum target of 24px.
- Do: Start the label with a verb that names the outcome. "Publish tokens" and "Approve change" tell the user what happens before they click.
- Do: One primary per view, the others step down. Hierarchy tells users where to look first. Secondary and ghost carry the alternatives.
- Do: Show progress with loading, keep the label. The button stays in place and focusable, so keyboard users do not lose their position. Change the label to the present participle.
- Do: A toggle says its state with pressed. Pass pressed true or false, never swap variants to show the state. The look, aria-pressed and a script driving a static page stay in step.
- Don't: Two primary buttons side by side. When everything is primary, nothing is. Users hesitate and pick at random.
- Don't: Vague labels. "OK" and "Click here" say nothing out of context, and screen reader users often list buttons out of context.
- Don't: Danger for actions that are not destructive. Red trains people to ignore red. Keep danger for actions that remove or revoke something.

### ButtonGroup

Lays out related buttons as one unit, either spaced (an action bar or dialog footer) or attached (a segmented control), and gives the group one accessible name.

- Family: Actions
- Tokens: border-width.default, space.2
- Use it for:
  - Footers of dialogs, forms and cards: primary at the end, alternatives before it.
  - Attached: two to five closely related choices of equal weight, like Unified or Split diff.
- Not for:
  - Switching between views of content: use Tabs, which manage the panel and arrow-key navigation.
  - A single choice that persists as a setting: use RadioGroup.
- Accessibility:
  - Renders role="group". Pass aria-label when the buttons are related choices so the group is announced.
  - Each button stays in the tab order; the focused button lifts above its neighbors so the ring is never clipped.
  - Vertical groups stack the same buttons; the tab order follows the visual order.
- Do: Put the primary action last. Users read the alternatives on the way to the main action, and the primary lands where the eye ends.
- Don't: Mix variants in an attached group. An attached group reads as one control. Mixed fills break it into unrelated pieces.

### IconButton

A square button with only an icon, for frequent, recognizable actions in toolbars, table rows and headers. Its label is still required: it becomes the accessible name.

- Family: Actions
- Tokens: border-width.default, border-width.strong, button.danger.bg, button.danger.bg-active, button.danger.bg-hover, button.danger.text, button.font-weight, button.ghost.bg-active, button.ghost.bg-hover, button.ghost.text, button.primary.bg, button.primary.bg-active, button.primary.bg-hover, button.primary.text, button.radius, button.secondary.bg, button.secondary.bg-active, button.secondary.bg-hover, button.secondary.border, button.secondary.text, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.control.checked.bg, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.surface.default, color.surface.hover, color.surface.pressed, color.surface.selected, color.text.default, color.text.link, color.text.link-hover, control.gap, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.lg, control.padding-x.md, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, ...
- Use it for:
  - Repeated row actions in tables and lists: edit, copy, delete, more.
  - Toolbars where space is tight and the icons are widely understood (close, copy, search, settings).
  - Opening a Menu of secondary actions (the more icon).
- Not for:
  - The primary action of a view: give it a text Button.
  - Any icon whose meaning is not obvious without its label: use a Button with iconStart instead.
  - Navigation to another page: use a Link.
- Accessibility:
  - label is required and becomes aria-label. The icon itself is aria-hidden.
  - Same keyboard behavior and focus ring as Button. Loading keeps focus and sets aria-busy.
  - The square target matches the control height (32/40/48 comfortable), never smaller than 24px.
- Do: Name the action, not the picture. label="Delete token" is what a screen reader says. "Trash" describes the drawing, not what happens.
- Do: Pair with a Tooltip showing the same label. Sighted mouse users get the name on hover; keyboard users get it on focus.
- Don't: A row of filled icon buttons. Primary icon buttons in every row shout. Keep row actions ghost.

### Link

Takes the user to another page, section or site. Underlined in running text so it is never identified by color alone.

- Family: Actions
- Tokens: border.width.1, border.width.2, color.border.strong, color.text.link, color.text.link-hover, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.inset, size.6, space.0-5
- Use it for:
  - Navigation: another page, a section of this page, an external resource.
  - Inline in sentences (inline variant), or on its own under a card or a table (standalone).
  - external for other sites: it opens a new tab and says so.
- Not for:
  - Actions on this screen (save, delete, open a dialog): use Button.
  - Navigation that should look like a button (a single call to action): use Button with render={<a href />}.
- Accessibility:
  - Native <a href>: Enter follows it, it is announced as a link, Cmd or Ctrl+click opens a new tab.
  - Inline links are underlined (WCAG 1.4.1): color is never the only cue inside text.
  - external adds target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer, an icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.
  - Focus ring hugs the text with a 1px offset so it does not overlap neighbouring lines.
- Do: Link text says where it goes. Screen reader users jump between links out of context: "Read the token guidelines" works alone, "here" does not.
- Don't: "Click here" or a bare URL. Both say nothing about the destination.

### Checkbox

A single on or off choice with its label next to the box, submitted with a form. Supports a mixed state for a parent that controls a partly checked group.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, checkbox.bg, checkbox.bg-checked, checkbox.border, checkbox.fg-checked, checkbox.radius, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.border.default, color.border.hover, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.regular, input.border-invalid, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.standard, size.4, size.6, space.0-5, space.2
- Use it for:
  - An independent yes or no that takes effect when the form is saved: agree, include, require.
  - Several independent options under one question: put them in a CheckboxGroup.
  - Selecting rows in a Table (with a parent checkbox in the header for select all).
- Not for:
  - A setting that applies immediately: use Switch.
  - One choice among exclusive options: use RadioGroup.
  - A command (Delete, Publish): use Button.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Checkbox: role checkbox, Space toggles, aria-checked is true, false or mixed (indeterminate).
  - The whole label row is the click target; the label text is the accessible name (aria-labelledby) and the description is linked with aria-describedby.
  - The box edge uses color.border.strong (3:1 against surfaces); checked uses the ink fill with a white check (4.5:1 or more).
  - Indeterminate shows a dash, so mixed is not conveyed by color.
  - invalid adds a danger edge; always pair it with an error message in the group or form.
- Do: Phrase the label as the positive case. Checked means the label is true. "Notify reviewers" reads cleanly; a negative label makes users double-check.
- Do: Use the description for consequences. Keep the label short and explain the effect underneath.
- Don't: Negative labels. "Do not send notifications" checked means off. Users have to think twice.
- Don't: A checkbox that acts immediately. If ticking it changes something right away, it is a Switch.

### CheckboxGroup

Several independent choices under one question, in a fieldset with a legend. An optional parent checkbox selects or clears the whole group and shows a mixed state.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.text, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, input.border-invalid, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.6
- Use it for:
  - Users may pick zero, one or several options from a short visible list (up to about seven).
  - Use allValues plus <Checkbox parent /> for a Select all at the top of a long list.
- Not for:
  - Only one option can be picked: use RadioGroup.
  - More than about seven options or a searchable list: use Combobox with multiple selection.
- Accessibility:
  - Native fieldset and legend: the legend names the group; disabled on the fieldset disables every item.
  - description and error are linked to the fieldset with aria-describedby; the error carries an icon and text.
  - The parent checkbox is checked, unchecked or mixed (aria-checked) based on the children, driven by Base UI.
  - Each item keeps its own label and description, so items can be reached and understood one by one.
- Do: Ask the question in the legend. The legend is read before each option, so it gives every label its context.
- Don't: A group without a legend. Screen reader users hear "Light, checkbox" with no idea what it is for.

### ChoiceCard

One choice among two to four options that each need a title and a short description, shown as cards: Keep mine or Use the library's, a starting brand, a corner style. The whole card is the click target.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, border.width.1, checkbox.bg, checkbox.bg-checked, checkbox.border, checkbox.fg-checked, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.border.hover, color.border.strong, color.control.checked.bg, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.text, color.surface.default, color.surface.hover, color.surface.selected, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, font.weight.semibold, input.border-invalid, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.standard, radius.control, ...
- Use it for:
  - A decision where each option needs a line of explanation or a value to compare: resolving a conflict, picking a starting brand.
  - Two to four options. Side by side (horizontal, the default) when the reader compares them; they stack on their own when they no longer fit.
  - vertical when the descriptions are long or the options are a ranked list.
  - Put a TokenValue in description when the choice is between token values, so the reader sees what each card keeps.
  - hideLabel when the row around the group already asks the question; the legend stays the accessible name.
- Not for:
  - Options a short label explains on its own: use RadioGroup.
  - Switching a view or a mode that applies at once: use SegmentedControl.
  - Several options the reader can pick together: use Checkbox.
  - More than four options: use RadioGroup or Select.
- Accessibility:
  - A fieldset with a legend around a Base UI RadioGroup: the legend names the group, each card is a radio named by its title.
  - Each card's description is linked to its radio with aria-describedby, so screen readers read it after the title. The group description and error are linked to the group.
  - Tab enters the group on the selected card and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection.
  - The selected card shows the checked radio, a Deep Harbor edge and the selected surface: never color alone.
  - A disabled card is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be picked; say why in its description.
  - The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on the radio on keyboard focus only.
- Do: Titles are the choice, descriptions are the consequence. The title says what the reader picks in a few words, the description says what happens or what it keeps.
- Do: Ask the question in the legend. The legend names the decision, as a question or a noun, so the cards read as answers.
- Don't: Cards for one-word options. When the titles say it all and nothing needs comparing, cards take room for nothing. Use RadioGroup.
- Don't: Descriptions that repeat the title. "Keep mine: keeps your value" says it twice. Show the value instead, or what changes.

### Combobox

A text input that filters a list of options as the user types, then selects one or several of them. Built for long lists and async search (people, repositories, tokens).

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.surface.hover, color.surface.hover-raised, color.surface.pressed, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.md, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.size.300, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, input.bg, input.bg-disabled, input.border, input.border-hover, input.border-invalid, input.placeholder, input.radius, input.text, layer.popover, menu.item-height, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, motion.easing.standard, popup.bg, ...
- Use it for:
  - Choosing from a long or growing list where typing is faster than scrolling: reviewers, repositories, components, tokens.
  - Results come from a server: control inputValue, fetch, pass the results as options with filter={null} and loading while waiting.
  - Several values from a long list (multiple): selected values become removable chips inside the field.
  - Inside a Dialog or Drawer: the list opens above the dialog and focus stays in it. Use description for a short second line under each label (12px, muted), like a component's family or a person's role.
- Not for:
  - Short known lists (under about ten): use Select, which needs no typing.
  - Free text with suggestions (a search box): the value must be one of the options here, so use Input or an autocomplete pattern.
  - Two or three options: use RadioGroup.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Combobox: the input has role combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the popup is a listbox.
  - Keyboard: typing filters; Down Arrow opens and moves; Enter selects; Escape closes, then clears; with multiple, Left Arrow from the start of the input moves through the chips and Backspace removes one.
  - loading renders the message in a live status region and sets aria-busy on the popup; the empty message is announced the same way.
  - The clear and toggle buttons inside the field have accessible names ("Clear selection", "Show options"); each chip remove button says "Remove <name>".
  - The Field label names the input; hint and error are linked through aria-describedby.
  - The popup is portaled and re-applies the theme, brand and density of its field. It sits on the popover layer, above a Dialog, and the dialog keeps focus management: picking returns focus to the input inside the dialog.
- Do: Add a second line when names are ambiguous. A role or an email under the name helps pick the right Ada, and is matched by screen readers too.
- Do: Write an empty message that says what to try. "No one matches. Check the spelling or invite them." turns a dead end into a next step.
- Don't: Spinner with no words. While loading, say what is happening ("Searching people"). The message is also announced to screen readers.
- Don't: Combobox for a handful of fixed options. Typing to find one of three themes is slower than seeing them. Use Select or RadioGroup.

### Field

Wires a visible label, an optional description and an error message to one form control. Ids, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and validation timing are handled by Base UI Field.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.text, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5
- Use it for:
  - Around every Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, NumberField or Slider that does not take a label prop itself.
  - To show a server-side error next to the right control (error prop, or Form errors by name).
  - description for what the user needs before typing: format, limits, why you ask.
- Not for:
  - Checkbox and Switch: they carry their own label next to the control.
  - A group of checkboxes or radios: use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup, which render a fieldset and legend.
- Accessibility:
  - The label is a native <label> bound to the control: clicking it focuses the control.
  - description and error are linked through aria-describedby; an error also sets aria-invalid on the control.
  - Errors carry an icon and text, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
  - required shows an asterisk (hidden from screen readers) and sets the native required attribute, which is announced.
  - hideLabel keeps the label for assistive tech; use it only when the context labels the field visually (a search bar with an icon).
- Do: Description before, error after. The description answers questions before typing; the error appears under the control, where the eye already is.
- Don't: Placeholder as the label. It disappears on the first keystroke and has low contrast. Keep a visible label.

### Form

A form with one validation pattern for the whole system: client checks on submit, server errors passed by field name, each shown under its Field and listed in a summary that takes focus.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, border.width.1, color.feedback.danger.bg, color.feedback.danger.border, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.text, color.text.default, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.200, font.weight.semibold, radius.container, radius.inset, space.0-5, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.5
- Use it for:
  - Any group of fields submitted together: connect a repository, create a token, invite reviewers.
  - errors for server-side validation, keyed by each Field's name.
  - FormActions for the button row: primary action last.
- Not for:
  - A single setting that saves on change: use Switch or an inline control without a form.
  - Search and filter bars that update results live: no submit, no Form.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Form: native form element; fields validate on submit and the first invalid field gets focus.
  - Server errors set aria-invalid on the control and are linked with aria-describedby.
  - The error summary is role alert, receives focus when new errors arrive, and links move focus to each field.
  - Errors are icon plus text, never color alone.
- Do: Validate on submit, then live. Do not flag fields while the user is still typing for the first time. After a failed submit, errors clear as soon as the value is fixed.
- Do: Keep what the user typed. Show the error next to the value so it can be corrected, never clear the field.
- Don't: Disabling submit until the form is valid. A disabled button explains nothing. Keep it enabled and show what is missing on submit.
- Don't: One generic error at the top. "Something went wrong" sends users hunting. Attach each error to its field.

### Input

Single-line text field with optional prefix and suffix. Give it a label prop for a complete field, or place it inside a Field.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.md, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, font.size.300, input.bg, input.bg-disabled, input.border, input.border-hover, input.border-invalid, input.placeholder, input.radius, input.text, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, space.2
- Use it for:
  - Short free text: a name, a URL, a search query, a value with a unit.
  - prefix for an icon or a currency, suffix for a unit or a keyboard hint.
  - size follows density: md in forms and in a page's filter bar, sm only in dense toolbars, menus and panels, lg only on sparse screens. In a filter bar the search field, its Select and its SegmentedControl share one size, so the row reads as one height.
- Not for:
  - More than one line: use Textarea.
  - Numbers with steps, min and max: use NumberField (increment buttons, arrow keys, locale formatting).
  - Choosing from a known list: Select for under about ten options, Combobox for long or searchable lists.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Input: inherits label, description and error wiring from the surrounding Field.
  - The field edge (color.border.strong) has at least 3:1 contrast with the surface in both themes (WCAG 1.4.11).
  - Focus shows a 2px signal-colored edge on every focus, since users type into it.
  - On touch screens the text is 17px so iOS does not zoom the page on focus.
  - A prefix icon is decorative; if the prefix carries meaning (a currency), make it text.
- Do: Label above, format help in the hint. The label stays visible while typing; the hint answers the question before it is asked.
- Do: Units in the suffix. The value stays a number the user can edit; the unit is context, not content.
- Don't: Clearing the value on error. Keep what the user typed and say how to fix it.

### NumberField

Numeric input with decrease and increase buttons, arrow-key stepping, min and max, and locale-aware formatting.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.border.default, color.surface.hover, color.surface.pressed, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.size.200, font.size.300, input.bg, input.bg-disabled, input.border, input.border-hover, input.border-invalid, input.radius, input.text, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, space.2
- Use it for:
  - Exact numbers within known bounds: approvals, columns, spacing steps, retry counts.
  - suffix for the unit (px, ms, %), format for currency or percent.
- Not for:
  - Identifiers that only look like numbers (zip codes, ids, phone numbers): use Input with inputMode numeric.
  - Rough values where position matters: use Slider.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI NumberField: a text input with role textbox and aria-roledescription Number field; Arrow Up and Down step, Shift uses largeStep.
  - The decrease and increase buttons are named and disabled at min and max.
  - Inherits label, description and error from Field; invalid sets aria-invalid and a danger edge.
  - Values use tabular figures so digits do not jump while stepping.
- Do: Set min and max. Bounds disable the buttons at the edges and stop impossible values.
- Don't: Unit in the label and in the value. Say it once, in the suffix: "Base spacing" with px, not "Base spacing (px)" plus px.

### RadioGroup

One choice among a few visible, mutually exclusive options. Arrow keys move the selection; the group has a legend and optional per-option descriptions.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, border.width.1, checkbox.bg, checkbox.bg-checked, checkbox.border, checkbox.fg-checked, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.border.default, color.border.hover, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.text, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, input.border-invalid, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.standard, radius.pill, size.4, size.6, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.6
- Use it for:
  - Two to about six exclusive options that benefit from being compared side by side.
  - Options that need a description to choose well.
  - horizontal only for two or three short options, like Light, Dark, System.
- Not for:
  - More than about six options, or options users know by name: use Select.
  - A single on or off: use Switch or Checkbox.
  - Switching views of content: use Tabs.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI RadioGroup: role radiogroup named by the legend; one tab stop, arrow keys move and select.
  - Each radio is labelled by its text (aria-labelledby) and described by its description.
  - The group error is linked with aria-describedby and sets aria-invalid; it shows an icon and text.
  - Selected uses the ink fill with a light dot; the unselected edge is color.border.strong (3:1).
- Do: Preselect the safest or most common option. A default saves a decision; pick the one most teams want.
- Don't: A single radio button. One radio cannot be unselected. Use a Checkbox.

### SegmentedControl

Picks one of a few views or modes, shown side by side as attached buttons: the brand of a preview, the density, light or dark. The choice applies at once, on the current screen.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.action.disabled.bg, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.control.checked.bg, color.control.checked.fg, color.surface.pressed, color.surface.raised, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.md, control.height.sm, elevation.raised, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.tight, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.control, radius.inset, space.0-5, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.8
- Use it for:
  - Switching how the same content is shown: Light or Dark, Comfortable or Compact, Grid or List.
  - Short options where seeing every option at once helps the choice: two to five usually, more for filters people switch between often (status filters). On a phone the track scrolls sideways and never widens the page.
  - Appearance strong when the control is what the view is about (the status filter of a list): the selected segment fills with Deep Harbor. At most one strong control per view.
  - The change applies immediately, with no Save button.
  - Size sm in dense toolbars, menus and panels; md everywhere else, including a page's filter bar, where it matches the md search field and Select beside it. Heights follow the density setting.
  - fullWidth inside a narrow panel or menu, so the segments share the width equally.
- Not for:
  - Switching between panels of different content: use Tabs, which link each tab to its panel.
  - A setting in a form that is saved later: use RadioGroup, which shows a label and help per option.
  - Long labels, or options people pick once and forget: use Select.
  - Turning one thing on or off: use Switch.
  - Triggering actions (Export, Delete): use Button or an attached ButtonGroup.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI RadioGroup with native button radios: role radiogroup on the row, role radio and aria-checked on each segment.
  - Tab enters the group on the selected segment and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection, Home and End jump to the ends.
  - Give the group a name: aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label outside the track, or label (aria-label) when the context already names it.
  - The selected segment is marked by a raised plate with a checked-color edge (or the Deep Harbor fill with strong) and a darker text color, not by color alone.
  - When the track scrolls, arrow keys still move the selection and the selected segment scrolls into view.
  - The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on keyboard focus only.
  - Rendered without JavaScript, the HTML keeps role, aria-checked and data-value, so a small script can drive it: flip aria-checked and tabindex, and handle arrow keys.
- Do: Short, parallel labels. One or two words per segment, same grammatical form, so the set reads as one choice.
- Do: Label outside the track. Put a visible label to the left of the track, as a caption on its center line, and name the group with it (aria-labelledby, or the same words in label). The track holds the options and nothing else.
- Do: Strong for the control the view is about. A list filtered by status: the selected filter fills with Deep Harbor, the strongest signal on the screen. Six short filters are fine; on a phone they scroll sideways.
- Do: Always start with a selection. A segmented control shows the current mode. Pass value or defaultValue so one segment is always selected.
- Don't: Actions dressed as segments. Segments select a mode; they never run a command. "Export" and "Share" belong on buttons.
- Don't: The label inside the track. Never put the group's label in the same pill as the options. Inside one container it reads as one more option ("Brand" next to "Bridge" and "Ocean"). Keep it outside, to the left.
- Don't: Too many or too long options. Two or three words per segment make the track longer than the screen and stop reading as one control. Keep labels to one or two words, or use Select.

### Select

Picks one value from a short, known list in a popup. The trigger looks like an Input so forms read as one family; the list supports groups, descriptions, badges and disabled options.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.surface.hover-raised, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, control.height.md, control.height.sm, control.padding-x.md, control.padding-x.sm, focus.ring.color, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.size.300, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, input.bg, input.bg-disabled, input.border, input.border-hover, input.border-invalid, input.placeholder, input.radius, input.text, layer.popover, menu.item-height, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, motion.easing.standard, popup.bg, popup.border, popup.radius, popup.shadow, ...
- Use it for:
  - One choice from about 4 to 10 known options: a theme, a brand, a token group, a role.
  - The options are long words or labels that would crowd a RadioGroup.
  - Space is tight: in a dense toolbar, a menu or a settings row (size sm). In a page's filter bar, size md, like the search field beside it.
  - Each option carries a short fact worth seeing before the pick, like a status or a count: put a Badge in badge. It shows on the item and in the trigger once selected.
- Not for:
  - Two or three options that should all stay visible: use RadioGroup, or an attached ButtonGroup for a view switch.
  - Long or unknown lists (people, repositories, 20+ tokens): use Combobox so users can type to filter.
  - Several values at once: use Combobox with multiple, or a CheckboxGroup.
  - Actions (Duplicate, Delete): use Menu. A Select changes a value, it does not run commands.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Select: the trigger is a combobox button with aria-expanded; the popup is a listbox with options marked aria-selected and aria-disabled.
  - Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow keys open it; arrows move; typing jumps to a matching option; Enter selects; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
  - The Field label names the trigger; hint and error are linked through aria-describedby, and an error sets aria-invalid.
  - The selected option shows a check mark and a medium weight, not color alone.
  - The trigger edge uses color.border.strong (3:1 against surfaces) and the signal focus ring on keyboard focus.
  - The popup is portaled and re-applies the theme, brand and density of its trigger.
- Do: A status next to the label with badge. A Badge in the option's badge slot says the status at a glance, in the list and in the trigger. The description stays for a second line of detail, like who made it.
- Do: Order options by meaning, not alphabetically by default. Put the most common choice first, or follow the natural order (System, Light, Dark). Group long lists under short headings.
- Do: Explain a disabled option. A description on the option says why it cannot be picked, instead of leaving users guessing.
- Don't: A Select with two options. Hiding two choices behind a click costs a step for nothing. Show them as radios or a Switch.
- Don't: The placeholder as an instruction. "Click to select" says nothing. The placeholder describes the empty state: "No theme", "Any reviewer".

### Slider

Picks a value or a range by position on a continuous scale, with the formatted value shown at the end of the track.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.strong, color.border.strong, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, elevation.raised, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.size.200, input.border-invalid, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.pill, size.20, size.4, size.6, slider.range, slider.thumb, slider.track, space.1, space.4
- Use it for:
  - Approximate values where the position matters more than the exact number: opacity, threshold, zoom.
  - A range with two thumbs: pass an array of two numbers.
  - Live previews: update on onValueChange, save on onValueCommitted.
- Not for:
  - An exact number the user knows: use NumberField.
  - Very large ranges where one step is tiny: pair it with a NumberField or use NumberField alone.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Slider: each thumb is a native range input with role slider, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext from format.
  - Arrow keys step, Page Up and Page Down or Shift+arrow use largeStep, Home and End jump to min and max.
  - Range thumbs are named "<label> minimum" and "<label> maximum"; override with thumbLabels.
  - The filled range uses the signal color (3:1 on the muted track); focus rings the thumb.
- Do: Show the value and its unit. format makes the value readable: 48%, 4.5, 16 px.
- Don't: A slider for precise input. Dragging to exactly 37 is frustrating. Use NumberField when the exact number matters.

### Switch

Turns a setting on or off with immediate effect, like a light switch. No save button needed.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: color.bg.muted, color.border.hover, color.border.strong, color.control.checked.bg-hover, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, elevation.raised, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, motion.duration.fast, motion.easing.standard, radius.pill, size.3, size.4, size.5, size.6, size.7, size.9, space.0-5, space.3, switch.thumb, switch.thumb-on, switch.track-off, switch.track-on
- Use it for:
  - Settings that apply as soon as they are flipped: notifications, auto-publish, preview mode.
  - labelPlacement start in settings lists, so labels align left and switches align right.
- Not for:
  - A choice saved later with a form button: use Checkbox.
  - More than two states: use RadioGroup or Select.
  - Starting an action (Publish, Sync): use Button.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Switch: role switch with aria-checked; Space and Enter toggle it; the label row is the click target.
  - The off track uses control.track (3:1 against surfaces) and the thumb keeps 3:1 against the track, so the state is visible without color.
  - The thumb position carries the state, not only the track color.
  - If flipping it fails (network), revert it and say why next to it.
- Do: Name the setting, not the state. The switch shows on or off; the label says what is on or off.
- Don't: Labels that change with the state. "On" and "Off" labels repeat what the control already shows and hide what it controls.
- Don't: A switch that waits for Save. Users expect a switch to act at once. Inside a form that saves later, use a Checkbox.

### Textarea

Multi-line text that grows with its content up to a maximum, with an optional character count. Give it a label prop or place it inside a Field.

- Family: Forms
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.surface.hover, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.padding-x.md, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.size.300, font.tracking.wide, input.bg, input.bg-disabled, input.border, input.border-hover, input.border-invalid, input.placeholder, input.radius, input.text, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.inset, space.0-5, space.1, space.2
- Use it for:
  - Free text longer than one line: pull request summaries, release notes, review comments.
  - showCount with maxLength when there is a hard limit.
  - appearance="inline" only to edit existing text in place, where the text is the page: a paragraph, a list item or a card title in a docs editor. It keeps the surrounding font, size and line height and shows a field on hover and focus.
- Not for:
  - A short single value: use Input.
  - Structured content (lists of tokens, key-value pairs): use dedicated fields.
  - appearance="inline" in a form, a dialog or a settings page: people scan forms for boxes, and an inline field there reads as plain text. Use the default field.
- Accessibility:
  - Native textarea through Base UI Field: label, description and error are wired for you.
  - Focus shows a 2px signal edge; invalid sets aria-invalid and a danger edge with a text error.
  - The visual counter is hidden from screen readers to avoid announcing every keystroke; maxLength is enforced natively.
  - On touch screens the text is 17px so iOS does not zoom on focus.
  - appearance="inline" is still a native, labelled textarea. Hover adds a fill and a hairline edge and focus the 2px DS ring, so the field never relies on color alone.
  - The inline placeholder uses the muted text color, checked at 4.5:1 on the canvas, surfaces and the hover fill.
  - Inline text inherits the page size, also on touch screens: keep the surrounding text at 16px or more so iOS does not zoom on focus.
- Do: Size it for the expected answer. rows sets the starting height; autosize grows it, so short boxes do not hide long answers.
- Do: Inline only where the text already is. Swap the paragraph or list item for an inline Textarea holding the same text, so the page keeps its layout while it is edited. Name each one with aria-label.
- Don't: Hiding the limit until it is hit. Show the count while typing so users can edit before the error.
- Don't: Inline fields in a form. Without a box, an empty form field reads as finished text. Forms use the default field with a visible label.

### Alert

An inline message about the state of a page or a section: a failed publish, a pending review, a sync in progress. It stays until the situation changes or the user dismisses it.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: alert.radius, border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.feedback.danger.bg, color.feedback.danger.border, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.info.bg, color.feedback.info.border, color.feedback.info.icon, color.feedback.success.bg, color.feedback.success.border, color.feedback.success.icon, color.feedback.warning.bg, color.feedback.warning.border, color.feedback.warning.icon, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.sm, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, font.weight.semibold, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.4
- Use it for:
  - A condition that affects what the user is doing here: a failed build, a protected branch, contrast warnings.
  - Tone follows meaning: danger for failed or blocked, warning for needs attention, success for a finished task that changed this page, info for context, neutral when there is no judgement.
  - Inside a form or card, above the content it is about.
  - actionsPlacement inline for one short message and one action, like a banner saying which change you are viewing with Back to latest at the end of the line. It wraps under the text on a phone. Keep below for a title plus a longer description.
- Not for:
  - Confirming an action the user just took (Copied, Saved): use a Toast.
  - An error on one field: use the Field error under that control.
  - A decision the user must make before continuing: use an AlertDialog.
- Accessibility:
  - Alerts that appear after load are announced: danger and warning with role="alert" (interrupts), the others with role="status" (polite).
  - Alerts present when the page loads should use announce="off": a live region on load is either ignored or read twice.
  - Every tone has its own icon and the text carries the meaning, so color is never the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1).
  - The dismiss button is a named IconButton (dismissLabel, default "Dismiss"). Move focus to a sensible place after dismissing if the alert had focus.
  - Feedback text and icon colors are checked against their tinted backgrounds in both themes.
- Do: Title says what happened, description says what to do. Users scan the bold line and read on only when they need to act.
- Do: Give the way out as an action. A button next to the problem saves a search through the page.
- Don't: Stacking several alerts. Three alerts in a row read as noise. Merge them, or keep the most severe and link to the rest.
- Don't: Danger for something that is not broken. Red trains people to ignore red. Use info or warning when nothing failed.

### Banner

A page-level mode banner: the page shows something other than usual, such as a past change of the library or an edit mode, and the way back sits on the same line. One per page, at the top of the content.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.surface.strong, color.text.default, color.text.muted, color.text.on-solid, control.height.md, font.family.sans, font.weight.semibold, icon.size.md, layer.sticky, layout.header.height, radius.container, size.60, space.0-5, space.2, space.3, space.4, typography.ui.line-height, typography.ui.size
- Use it for:
  - The whole page is in a mode the reader must not forget: previewing a past change, editing guidelines, viewing as another brand.
  - Give the way out as an action on the same line ("Back to latest library"), a Button with size sm and variant secondary, and at most one more action. On narrow screens the actions go under the text and fill the row.
  - strong (default, Deep Harbor) for a mode the whole page is in; neutral for a quieter, scoped mode such as an editor.
  - sticky="top" or sticky="below-header" when the page scrolls long, so the way back stays in view.
- Not for:
  - A message about the page's content (a failed build, a contrast warning): use Alert.
  - Confirming an action the user just took: use a Toast.
  - Marketing or announcements: Banner is for a state the page is in, not for news.
  - More than one per page: merge the modes into one sentence, or pick the one that matters.
- Accessibility:
  - A landmark region named by its title (role region, aria-labelledby), so screen reader users find the mode in the landmarks list.
  - Not a live region: the banner is part of the page when it loads. If a mode starts without a page load, move focus to the banner title or announce the mode once.
  - The actions are real Buttons on the same line as the title, reached with Tab right after the title.
  - The strong appearance uses color.surface.strong (Deep Harbor in both themes) with color.text.on-solid, 8.87:1, and the focus ring inside it takes the text color. The icon and the words carry the mode, never color alone.
  - Sticky banners stay under the app header (layout.header.height) and above the content (layer.sticky), so they never hide the header's controls.
- Do: Say the mode and its consequence in one sentence. What the reader sees and what it means for their work: "Viewing the library as change #118. Nothing is saved."
- Do: Neutral for a scoped mode. An edit mode on one part of the page does not need the strong color. Keep Deep Harbor for modes the whole page is in.
- Don't: A banner for news. "New components are available" is not a mode. It belongs in a changelog or an Alert, not in the strong band at the top of the page.
- Don't: A vague mode. "Preview mode" does not say what is previewed or whether work is saved. Name the object and the consequence.

### EmptyState

Explains why a view has no content yet and invites the action that fills it. An empty screen is a starting point, not a dead end.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.border.default, color.surface.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.line-height.tight, font.size.200, font.size.300, font.size.400, font.size.600, font.tracking.snug, font.tracking.tight, font.weight.semibold, radius.container, radius.control, size.10, size.12, size.14, space.1, space.1-5, space.10, space.16, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.5, space.6
- Use it for:
  - First use: nothing has been created yet (no tokens, no pull requests). Explain the value and offer the first step.
  - No results: a search or filter matched nothing. Say what was searched and how to widen it.
  - Cleared: the user finished everything (no reviews waiting). Confirm it calmly.
  - size sm inside tables and cards, md in panels, lg for a whole page.
- Not for:
  - Errors that stopped content from loading: use an Alert with a retry action.
  - Content still loading: use Skeleton.
- Accessibility:
  - The title is a real heading (headingLevel, default h3) so it appears in the page outline; pick the level that fits the page.
  - The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title carries the meaning.
  - Actions are regular Buttons or Links in the tab order, after the text.
- Do: Say what goes here and how to get it. The title names the missing object, the description says where it comes from, the button starts it.
- Don't: "Nothing here" with no way forward. It describes the screen the user already sees and leaves them stuck.

### Progress

Shows how far a task has gone: a linear bar in layouts, a circular ring in compact spots. Indeterminate when the duration is unknown.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.success.icon, color.feedback.warning.icon, color.text.default, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.moderate, motion.duration.shimmer, motion.duration.spin, motion.easing.standard, progress.fill, progress.track, radius.pill, size.14, size.5, size.8, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.3
- Use it for:
  - Tasks that take more than about two seconds and report progress: publishing, importing from Figma, running contrast checks.
  - Indeterminate (value null) when the task runs but its length is unknown.
  - Switch tone to success or danger when the task ends, and say so in the label.
- Not for:
  - Short waits or busy controls: use Spinner (or Button loading).
  - Content that is loading into a layout: use Skeleton in the shape of the content.
  - A static measurement like storage used or a score: that is a meter, not progress.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Progress: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax; indeterminate drops aria-valuenow.
  - Needs a name: the label prop, or aria-label when there is no visible label (rings).
  - The visible value text is aria-hidden; screen readers get it from aria-valuetext (customize with getAriaValueText).
  - The fill uses the signal color with at least 3:1 against the track and surfaces.
  - Under reduced motion the indeterminate bar stops sliding and shows a full, softened track instead.
- Do: Label the task, show the value. "Publishing tokens 64%" tells users what is happening and how long is left.
- Do: Use counts when they mean more than percent. getAriaValueText and the label can say "12 of 40 pairs".
- Don't: A progress bar that never moves. If you cannot report progress, use the indeterminate state rather than a fake value.

### Skeleton

A placeholder in the shape of content that is loading, so the layout does not jump when the data arrives.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: motion.duration.shimmer, motion.easing.standard, radius.container, radius.pill, size.10, size.20, skeleton.base, skeleton.radius, skeleton.shine
- Use it for:
  - First load of a list, table, card or detail panel whose shape you know.
  - Mirror the real layout: a circle for an avatar, short lines for names, a block for a preview.
  - Pair with aria-busy="true" on the region and a visually hidden "Loading tokens".
- Not for:
  - Inside a button or after a click on a control: use Button loading or Spinner.
  - Long tasks with known progress: use Progress.
  - When loading takes under about 300 ms: show nothing, the flash is worse than the wait.
- Accessibility:
  - Skeletons are always aria-hidden: they are decoration, not content.
  - Put aria-busy="true" on the loading region and a VisuallyHidden label like "Loading tokens"; remove both when the content arrives.
  - The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion; use static for long lists.
- Do: Match the shape of the real content. The page settles in place instead of reflowing when data lands.
- Don't: A whole page of shimmering blocks. Load the frame (navigation, titles) for real and use skeletons only where the data goes.

### Spinner

An indeterminate activity indicator for short waits and busy controls. For content that is loading into a layout, use Skeleton; for long tasks, use Progress.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: color.signal.default, icon.size.lg, icon.size.md, icon.size.sm, icon.size.xs, motion.duration.spin
- Use it for:
  - Inside a control that is working: Button and IconButton show it automatically with loading.
  - Small regions that refresh in place, for waits up to a few seconds.
  - tone signal when it stands alone, current when it sits in text or a control.
- Not for:
  - First load of a list or a page: use Skeleton in the shape of the content.
  - Tasks with measurable progress or that take longer than a few seconds: use Progress.
- Accessibility:
  - With label it renders role="status" and is announced; without label it is aria-hidden (use it inside a control that sets aria-busy).
  - Under reduced motion it keeps turning, slower: a frozen spinner looks like a crash.
  - The arc is drawn in currentColor or the signal color, which keeps 3:1 against surfaces.
- Do: Name what is loading. A standalone spinner needs a label so screen readers hear "Loading tokens".
- Don't: A spinner in the middle of an empty page. It hides the layout and makes the wait feel longer. Show the frame and use skeletons.

### Toast

A short, temporary notification that confirms what just happened (Tokens published, Link copied) without interrupting. Shown with useToast() under a ToastProvider.

- Family: Feedback
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.info.icon, color.feedback.success.icon, color.feedback.warning.icon, color.text.default, color.text.muted, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, font.weight.semibold, layer.toast, motion.duration.moderate, motion.duration.slow, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, motion.easing.standard, size.96, space.0-5, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.6, toast.bg, toast.border, toast.radius, toast.shadow
- Use it for:
  - Confirming an action the user just took, especially when its result is not visible on screen: Copied, Published, Invitation sent.
  - Offering a quick reversal: Token deleted, with Undo.
  - Background work that finishes later: toast.promise() shows loading, then success or error.
- Not for:
  - Information the user must read or act on to continue: use an inline Alert or an AlertDialog.
  - Errors in a form: show them next to the fields.
  - Anything that needs more than one action or a long explanation.
- Accessibility:
  - Toasts render in a labelled region ("Notifications") that users reach with F6. Hovering or focusing the stack expands it and pauses auto dismiss.
  - Titles and descriptions are announced through a live region: politely by default, assertively for danger (priority high).
  - Toasts with an action, loading toasts and danger toasts from promise() do not auto dismiss, so screen reader and keyboard users have time to act.
  - Close and action buttons are real buttons with names; the close button is labelled "Dismiss notification".
  - Swipe right or down dismisses on touch. Under reduced motion toasts appear and leave without sliding.
- Do: Use the verb of the action, in the past tense. The button said Publish, the toast says Published. The vocabulary follows the flow.
- Do: Offer Undo for destructive actions. A toast with an action stays until the user acts or dismisses it, so nobody misses the way back.
- Don't: A toast for every click. If the result is visible on screen, the screen already confirms it.

### AlertDialog

Stops the user to confirm an action with consequences, usually destructive: delete tokens, revoke access, force publish. It asks one question and offers two answers.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.sm, dialog.bg, dialog.radius, dialog.scrim, dialog.shadow, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, layer.modal, layer.overlay, layout.inset, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.moderate, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, motion.easing.standard, size.140, size.180, size.96, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.6, typography.h3.family, typography.h3.line-height, typography.h3.size, typography.h3.tracking, typography.h3.weight
- Use it for:
  - Before an action that cannot be undone or that affects other people: deleting, revoking, overwriting.
  - tone primary for consequential but safe actions, like publishing a release to every consumer.
- Not for:
  - Actions that can be undone: do them right away and offer Undo in a Toast.
  - Collecting input: use Dialog.
  - Routine saves: confirmation fatigue teaches people to click through without reading.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI AlertDialog: role alertdialog, named by the title, described by the consequence.
  - Focus starts on Cancel, the safe choice, so a reflexive Enter does not destroy anything.
  - It does not close on an outside click; Escape and Cancel close it and focus returns to the trigger.
  - While loading, the confirm button keeps focus and announces aria-busy.
- Do: Ask a question that names the action and the object. "Delete 3 tokens?" with a confirm button "Delete tokens" is understood without reading the description.
- Do: Say the consequence, including what cannot be undone. "Components that use them fall back to their defaults. This cannot be undone."
- Don't: "Are you sure?" with Yes and No. It hides what is about to happen. Name the action in the title and on the button.

### Dialog

A modal window for a short, focused task that must be finished or cancelled before the user goes back to the page: rename a token, invite a reviewer, review a release.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.sm, dialog.bg, dialog.radius, dialog.scrim, dialog.shadow, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, layer.modal, layer.overlay, layout.inset, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.moderate, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, motion.easing.standard, size.140, size.180, size.96, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.6, typography.h3.family, typography.h3.line-height, typography.h3.size, typography.h3.tracking, typography.h3.weight
- Use it for:
  - A task of one to three fields that belongs to the current page and needs the user's full attention.
  - Reviewing something before committing it, like release notes before Publish.
  - Size sm for one field, md (default) for short forms, lg for reading or comparing content.
  - Plain-script pages without React render it with dialogHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom and call bindDialogs() once: the same look, focus trap, Escape, scrim and focus return. Never a homemade modal or a restyled native dialog.
- Not for:
  - Confirming a destructive action: use AlertDialog, which cannot be dismissed by clicking outside.
  - Details the user wants to read next to the page, like a token's history: use Drawer.
  - A hint or a small menu anchored to a control: use Popover or Menu.
  - Long multi-step flows: give them a page. Stacked dialogs lose people.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Dialog: role dialog, aria-modal, named by the title and described by the description.
  - Focus moves into the dialog when it opens (the first focusable element, or initialFocus) and is trapped there.
  - Escape, the close button and a click on the scrim close it; focus returns to the trigger.
  - The page behind is inert and scroll is locked while the dialog is open.
  - The body scrolls on its own when content is long, so the title and the actions stay visible.
  - Motion is a 200ms fade and a slight rise; with reduced motion it appears instantly.
- Do: Title says the task, the primary button repeats the verb. "Rename token" opens a dialog titled "Rename token" whose primary action is "Rename token". Users always know where they are.
- Do: Keep the footer for actions only. Alternatives first, primary last, aligned to the end. Explanations go in the description or the body.
- Don't: A dialog for information the page could show inline. Interrupting to say "Saved" costs a click. Use a Toast or an inline Alert.
- Don't: Vague footer labels. "OK" and "Yes" make users reread the title to know what they agree to.

### Drawer

A sheet that slides in from an edge and keeps the page in view behind it: token details, filters, a review checklist. On touch it can be swiped away.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.border.strong, color.text.default, color.text.muted, dialog.scrim, drawer.bg, drawer.border, drawer.radius, drawer.shadow, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, layer.modal, layer.overlay, layout.inset, motion.duration.instant, motion.duration.moderate, motion.duration.slow, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, radius.pill, size.10, size.120, size.160, size.80, space.1, space.12, space.2, space.24, space.3, typography.h3.family, typography.h3.line-height, typography.h3.size, typography.h3.tracking, typography.h3.weight
- Use it for:
  - Details or editing for one item of a list or table, where the user wants to keep the list in mind.
  - Filters and settings for the current view.
  - side end (default) for details, start for navigation, bottom for small screens and quick choices.
- Not for:
  - A short task that needs full attention: use Dialog.
  - Content that should stay visible while the user works on the page: use a non-modal side panel in the layout.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Drawer: modal dialog semantics, named by the title, focus trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.
  - Swipe to dismiss is an extra for touch, never the only way: the close button and Escape always work.
  - The page behind is inert while the drawer is open.
  - When the body is taller than the sheet it becomes a focusable region named by the title, so keyboard users can Tab to it and scroll with the arrow keys. A body that fits adds no tab stop.
  - Slides in 300ms with an exponential ease-out; reduced motion shows it instantly.
  - start and end follow the physical left and right in v1; RTL layouts should pass the mirrored side.
- Do: Title it with the item's name. "color.signal.default" tells the user which row they opened. The description says what it is for.
- Do: Put the actions in the footer. The footer stays visible while the body scrolls.
- Don't: A drawer that opens another drawer. Stacked sheets hide where the user came from. Navigate inside the drawer or use a page.

### Menu

A list of actions or options that opens from a button: row overflow actions, view options, sort order. Supports icons, shortcuts, groups, checkable items and submenus.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: border-width.default, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.mono, font.family.sans, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, icon.size.sm, layer.popover, menu.item-height, menu.item.bg-highlight, menu.item.indicator, menu.item.text, menu.item.text-danger, menu.item.text-disabled, menu.item.text-muted, menu.separator, motion.duration.fast, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, popup.bg, popup.border, popup.radius, popup.shadow, radius.pill, size.60, size.80, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.4
- Use it for:
  - More than two or three actions on one item: show the main one as a button and the rest in a Menu.
  - View options: checkable items for columns, a radio group for sort order.
  - A submenu for one level of grouping (Move to group, then the groups).
  - Leading icons when they help scanning (Rename, Duplicate, Delete): pass icon, a Lucide icon or an element like a brand mark. Put icons on every item of the menu or on none; labels stay aligned either way.
- Not for:
  - Choosing a value for a form field: use Select or Combobox, which work with Field and forms.
  - Navigation between pages: use links in the sidebar or tabs.
  - Two actions: show both as buttons.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Menu: the trigger has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; the popup is role menu with menuitem, menuitemcheckbox and menuitemradio children.
  - ArrowDown or Enter opens it and focuses the first item; arrows move, Home and End jump, typing a letter jumps to a matching item.
  - Enter and Space activate; checkable items toggle aria-checked and keep the menu open.
  - ArrowRight opens a submenu, ArrowLeft and Escape close it; Escape on the root returns focus to the trigger.
  - Shortcut hints are visual only (aria-hidden); bind the shortcut yourself and document it elsewhere.
  - Disabled items stay in the list so users learn the action exists, but cannot be activated.
- Do: Destructive items last, after a separator. Distance from routine actions prevents slips. The danger tone backs up the verb.
- Do: Icons on all items or on none. Labels stay aligned either way, but a mix reads as noise.
- Don't: Submenus inside submenus. Two levels deep loses keyboard and pointer users alike. Flatten with groups.

### Popover

A small non-modal panel anchored to a trigger, for extra detail or a quick choice that does not deserve a dialog: who must review, what a check does, branch info.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.200, font.weight.semibold, layer.popover, motion.duration.fast, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, popup.bg, popup.border, popup.radius, popup.shadow, size.80, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.4
- Use it for:
  - Explaining something next to the control it is about, when the text is too long for a tooltip or contains a link.
  - A small form or a couple of actions tied to one control.
  - Info icons: Popover (click or openOnHover) instead of Tooltip, so touch and screen reader users can reach it.
- Not for:
  - A list of actions: use Menu, which has the right keyboard model.
  - A label for an icon button: use Tooltip.
  - A task that must be completed or cancelled: use Dialog.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Popover: the trigger exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls; the popup is a dialog named by its title.
  - Focus moves into the popup when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. Escape and outside clicks close it.
  - Non-modal by default: the page stays usable. Set modal when the popover holds a small form.
  - It flips and shifts to stay in the viewport; the arrow follows the anchor.
- Do: Keep it short and anchored. A title, two sentences, at most one or two actions. The arrow shows what it belongs to.
- Don't: Forms that span several sections. A popover closes on an outside click, so long input gets lost. Use a Dialog or a Drawer.

### Tooltip

A short label that appears on hover and keyboard focus. It names icon buttons and reveals truncated text for sighted users; the accessible name always lives on the trigger.

- Family: Overlays
- Tokens: elevation.overlay, font.family.sans, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, layer.tooltip, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.exit, size.72, space.1, space.2, tooltip.bg, tooltip.radius, tooltip.text
- Use it for:
  - Every IconButton, with the same text as its label.
  - Truncated text, to show the full value.
  - Wrap the app once in TooltipProvider so neighbouring tooltips open instantly after the first one.
