  - Plain-script pages without React put tooltipAttributes() from @bridge-ds/react/dom on the trigger and call bindTooltips() once: the same tooltip, delay and keyboard behavior. Never a homemade data-tip tooltip: the design system audit counts those as look-alikes.
- Not for:
  - Information users need to complete a task: show it inline or in a Popover. Tooltips are invisible on touch screens.
  - Interactive content (links, buttons): tooltips cannot be reached. Use Popover.
  - Repeating a visible label: it adds noise.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI treats tooltips as visual labels: the trigger must carry the accessible name (IconButton label), which screen readers announce. The popup is not announced.
  - Opens on hover after the provider delay (500ms) and immediately on keyboard focus; Escape dismisses it.
  - The trigger must be focusable: wrap a Button, IconButton or Link, never plain text.
  - Inverse surface (tooltip.bg, tooltip.text) passes 4.5:1 in both themes.
- Do: Match the trigger's label. IconButton label="Copy token name" and the tooltip "Copy token name": what users see and hear is the same.
- Don't: Tooltips on disabled buttons to explain why. Disabled buttons do not receive focus, so keyboard users never see it. Explain inline instead.

### Breadcrumb

Shows where the current page sits in the library hierarchy and links back to each level above it.

- Family: Navigation
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.surface.hover, color.text.default, color.text.muted, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.snug, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.inset, size.6, size.60, space.1
- Use it for:
  - Pages two or more levels deep in a hierarchy: a token inside a group, a component inside a family.
  - At the top of the page, above the page title.
  - maxItems on deep paths so the trail stays on one line; the middle levels stay one click away.
- Not for:
  - Flat sites or the top level: there is nothing to go back up to.
  - Showing the steps of a flow: use a stepper. A breadcrumb shows location, not progress.
  - As the only navigation: it complements SidebarNav, it does not replace it.
- Accessibility:
  - A nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" (override with aria-label), with an ordered list inside.
  - The last item has aria-current="page".
  - Separators are icons hidden from assistive tech, so screen readers only read the levels.
  - The collapse button is named "Show N more levels" and expands the trail in place.
  - Truncated labels keep the full text in the title attribute and in the accessible name.
- Do: Mirror the hierarchy, not the history. Each item is a parent of the next, whatever route the user took to get here.
- Don't: Linking the current page. The last item is where the user already is. It is text with aria-current, not a link.

### Pagination

Moves through a long list split into pages, like the token table or the review history. The first and last pages stay visible; the rest collapse into ellipses.

- Family: Navigation
- Tokens: border-width.default, button.ghost.bg-active, button.ghost.bg-hover, color.control.checked.bg, color.control.checked.fg, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.md, control.height.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.size.200, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.control, space.1, space.2
- Use it for:
  - Long, stable lists where users need to know where they are and jump back: token tables, audit logs.
  - Below the list it controls, aligned with the list's start or end edge.
  - compact in narrow spaces (side panels, mobile) and in card footers.
- Not for:
  - Feeds the user skims once: load more or infinite scroll fit better.
  - Fewer than about 25 items: show them all.
  - Steps of a task: use a stepper.
- Accessibility:
  - A nav landmark named "Pagination" (override with aria-label when a page has several).
  - The current page button has aria-current="page" and an ink fill, not color alone.
  - Page buttons are named "Page N"; previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page" and are disabled at the ends.
  - Ellipses are icons hidden from assistive tech.
  - In compact, the "Page 3 of 12" text is a polite live region, so page changes are announced.
- Do: Keep the page in the URL. Reloading or sharing the link should land on the same page. Control page and onPageChange from your router.
- Don't: Hiding previous and next at the ends. Disabled previous on page 1 keeps the layout still and tells the user they are at the start.

### SidebarNav

The app's side navigation: sections of links to the main areas of Bridge, with the current page marked by a signal mark and an ink label.

- Family: Navigation
- Tokens: border-width.indicator, color.bg.muted, color.text.default, color.text.muted, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, menu.item-height, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.instant, motion.duration.moderate, motion.easing.enter, motion.easing.standard, nav.indicator, nav.item-bg-active, nav.item-bg-hover, radius.control, radius.pill, size.7, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.5
- Use it for:
  - Primary navigation of an app with more than five areas, in a left rail that stays visible.
  - Group items into titled sections by task (Library, Governance, Workspace).
  - collapsible on sections users rarely need, so the rail stays short.
  - count for items that need attention, like reviews waiting for you.
- Not for:
  - Switching views inside one page: use Tabs.
  - Fewer than five destinations: a top bar is enough.
  - Actions (Create token, Sync from Figma): put them in the page header as Buttons, not in the navigation.
- Accessibility:
  - A nav landmark: give it an aria-label when the page has other navigation (Breadcrumb, Pagination).
  - Each section is a list labelled by its title.
  - The current item has aria-current="page". It also gets a 2px signal mark and ink text, so color is not the only cue.
  - Collapsible section titles are buttons with aria-expanded (Base UI Collapsible); Enter and Space toggle them.
  - Items are full-width targets at the menu item height (36px comfortable, 30px compact).
- Do: Mark exactly one current page. active on the item for the current URL, including when the user is on a child page of it.
- Don't: Icons on some items only. A ragged column of icons breaks the scan line. Use icons on every item of a section or none.

### Tabs

Switches between views of the same object without leaving the page: the tokens, components and reviews of one library. The selected tab is marked with the signal underline.

- Family: Navigation
- Tokens: border-width.default, border-width.indicator, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.surface.default, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, control.height.md, control.height.sm, elevation.raised, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.tight, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.weight.medium, layout.gap, motion.duration.instant, motion.duration.moderate, motion.easing.standard, radius.container, radius.control, radius.pill, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.5, tabs.indicator, tabs.text, tabs.text-active
- Use it for:
  - Two to seven peer views of the same context, where users switch back and forth.
  - underline for page and card sections; contained for a compact switch inside a toolbar (Light or Dark preview).
  - count to show how many items wait in a view, like open reviews.
  - Vertical orientation for settings pages with many sections next to their content.
- Not for:
  - Steps of a sequence the user must complete in order: use a stepper or a form with sections.
  - Navigation between pages with their own URL: use SidebarNav or links styled as tabs, not Tabs (which do not change the URL).
  - Changing a setting or filter value: use RadioGroup or an attached ButtonGroup.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Tabs: role tablist, tab and tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby are wired for you.
  - One tab stop for the whole list. Arrow keys move between tabs (Up and Down when vertical), Home and End jump, focus wraps by default.
  - By default arrows move focus and Enter or Space selects; set activateOnFocus when panels are cheap to render.
  - Give the TabsList an aria-label (or labelledby) so the tablist has a name.
  - The selected tab has a visible signal underline plus stronger text: never color alone.
  - Disabled tabs are announced as disabled and cannot be selected.
- Do: Short, parallel labels. One or two nouns per tab, same grammatical form. The user scans them as a set.
- Don't: Tabs that are really actions. "Export" or "Delete" in a tab list hides an action behind a view switch. Use a Button.

### Accordion

Stacked sections that expand in place. Lets users scan headings and open only what they need.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: accordion.bg-hover, accordion.border, accordion.icon, accordion.text, border-width.default, color.border.strong, color.text.default, color.text.disabled, color.text.muted, control.height.lg, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.weight.medium, font.weight.regular, layout.inset, motion.duration.instant, motion.duration.moderate, motion.easing.standard, radius.container, space.2, space.3
- Use it for:
  - Long reference content where users look for one section: token groups, FAQ, advanced settings.
  - multiple when users compare sections; single (default) when sections are alternatives.
  - flush inside a card or a side panel, contained on a page.
- Not for:
  - Content everyone needs: do not hide it behind a click.
  - Switching between views of the same data: use Tabs.
  - Steps in a sequence: use a stepped layout with headings.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Accordion: each trigger is a button inside a heading (headingLevel, default h3) with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
  - Panels are regions labelled by their trigger. Enter and Space toggle; Tab moves between triggers.
  - Disabled items stay visible but cannot open.
  - The height animation uses motion tokens and collapses to 0ms with reduced motion.
- Do: Headings that work as a table of contents. Users scan the closed state. Name each section by its content, and show a count in meta when it helps.
- Don't: Nesting accordions. A collapsible inside a collapsible hides content twice. Flatten the structure or split the page.

### Avatar

A person, a team or Claude, shown as a photo with an initials or illustrated fallback. AvatarGroup stacks several and collapses the rest into a +N counter.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: avatar.agent-bg, avatar.agent-border, avatar.bg, avatar.illustrated-bg, avatar.ring, avatar.text, border-width.default, border.width.2, color.action.primary.bg, color.bg.subtle, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.none, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.weight.semibold, radius.inset, radius.pill, size.10, size.4, size.5, size.6, size.7, size.8
- Use it for:
  - Owners, reviewers and authors next to tokens, components and changes.
  - fallback="illustrated" when most people have no photo: a drawn face from their login tells rows apart faster than two letters. Import Avatar from @bridge-ds/react/avatar-illustrated (the drawings are a separate entry, about 120 kB gzipped).
  - kind="agent" brand="claude" for work Claude did (a drafted text, a change it opened): the Bridge agent mark (the Field Guide robot: a rounded head with an antenna, dot eyes and a smile) on a rounded square tile, named "Claude AI", so people see at a glance it is not a person.
  - mark only to show a vendor logo you have the brand owner's approval to use: Bridge ships its own agent mark because company logos are trademarks that need their owner's approval.
  - AvatarGroup for the reviewers of a change; set max so the row never wraps.
- Not for:
  - As the only way to identify someone in a table: write the name too.
  - For product or brand logos: use an image with its own alt text. The agent preset only attributes an agent's actions.
  - To make up a face for someone who has a photo: the illustration is a fallback, the photo wins.
- Accessibility:
  - role img with the full name as its label; initials and drawings are hidden from screen readers so they do not spell letters or describe a face.
  - The Claude preset is named "Claude AI"; its mark (the Bridge robot or a custom mark) is decorative inside it.
  - The robot is one stroke in currentColor with no fill, so it keeps the tile's checked contrast in light and dark, and still reads at the xs size (16px mark).
  - decorative removes it from the accessibility tree when the name is already written next to it.
  - The image has an empty alt: the name is on the container. Broken images fall back to initials or the drawing (Base UI Avatar).
  - AvatarGroup is a named group; the +N counter is announced as "3 more: names".
- Do: Name next to the avatar in lists. Faces are hard to tell apart at 24px. Mark the avatar decorative when the name is right beside it.
- Do: Seed with something stable. Seed the illustrated face with the login, not the display name: people rename themselves, their face should stay.
- Don't: Ten avatars in a row. Past four or five faces nobody counts. Let the +N counter carry the rest.
- Don't: Claude dressed as a person. Do not give Claude a drawn face or initials. Use the agent preset so nobody mistakes its work for a teammate's.

### Badge

A short, non-interactive status label like Draft, Published or Failed. The words carry the meaning; the tone reinforces it.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.border.default, color.feedback.danger.bg, color.feedback.danger.border, color.feedback.danger.icon, color.feedback.danger.solid, color.feedback.danger.text, color.feedback.info.bg, color.feedback.info.border, color.feedback.info.icon, color.feedback.info.solid, color.feedback.info.text, color.feedback.neutral.bg, color.feedback.success.bg, color.feedback.success.border, color.feedback.success.icon, color.feedback.success.solid, color.feedback.success.text, color.feedback.warning.bg, color.feedback.warning.border, color.feedback.warning.icon, color.feedback.warning.solid, color.feedback.warning.text, color.surface.inverse, color.text.default, color.text.inverse, color.text.muted, color.text.on-solid, font.family.sans, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, radius.pill, size.5, size.6, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, typography.caption.line-height, typography.caption.size, ...
- Use it for:
  - The status of one item in a table row, a list or a card header.
  - subtle (default) in lists and tables where many badges sit together; solid for the single status that must win a glance (Breaking, Build failed).
  - Tone by meaning: success done or healthy, warning needs attention, danger failed or blocked, info new or changed, neutral no judgement.
  - Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use badgeHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup, tones and sizes, without React. Never a homemade pill: the design system audit counts those as look-alikes.
- Not for:
  - Anything clickable or removable: use Tag.
  - A sentence or an explanation: use an inline Alert.
  - Counts on icons: use the number in text next to the label.
- Accessibility:
  - Static text read in reading order. No role, not focusable.
  - Subtle tones use feedback text on feedback bg (4.5:1); solid tones use text.on-solid on feedback solid (4.5:1). Checked by the token build in every brand and theme.
  - The dot and icon are decorative; the text carries the status.
  - If a status changes while the user watches (Running to Failed), announce it with a live region; the badge itself is silent.
- Do: The text says the status, the tone backs it up. Someone who cannot tell green from red still reads Published and Failed.
- Do: Subtle in rows, solid for the exception. A table full of solid badges shouts. Keep solid for the one thing that must stand out.
- Don't: Color as the only signal. A dot without words fails WCAG 1.4.1 and means nothing to a screen reader.
- Don't: A tone that contradicts the words. Danger for New borrows urgency the user did not ask for.

### Card

A flat plate with a hairline edge that groups related content: a release, a component summary, a settings section. It does not cast a shadow unless the whole card is one link.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, border.width.1, card.bg, card.border, card.radius, card.shadow, color.bg.subtle, color.border.hover, color.text.default, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.200, layout.inset, motion.duration.fast, motion.easing.standard, space.2, space.3, space.4, typography.h3.family, typography.h3.line-height, typography.h3.size, typography.h3.tracking, typography.h3.weight
- Use it for:
  - A self-contained unit the user scans or compares: a release, a component, a token group, an owner.
  - interactive when the whole card goes to one place (a component page): mark its title link with data-card-primary.
  - padding none for a full-bleed Table or media inside the card; compact in dense dashboards.
- Not for:
  - As the page structure: rows of identical cards are a lazy layout. Use headings, lists and tables first.
  - Inside another card: nested plates blur hierarchy. Use a Divider or a heading.
  - Floating content (menus, popovers): those are overlays with elevation, not cards.
- Accessibility:
  - A card is a plain div. Pass aria-labelledby pointing at its title when it should be a navigable group.
  - Interactive cards keep a real link (data-card-primary) whose text names the destination; its click area is stretched over the card and its focus ring moves to the card edge.
  - Other buttons inside an interactive card stay on top and remain separately focusable.
  - The hover lift is skipped when the user prefers reduced motion.
- Do: One primary action in the footer. The footer is for the decision; secondary actions step down to ghost.
- Don't: A card around a single sentence. A box with one line adds noise. Let the text sit on the page.

### Checklist

The steps or conditions something needs, one row each: a status icon, a title, one line of detail and, when there is one, the action on the same row. Like the merge box of a pull request.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, border-width.strong, color.border.default, color.border.emphasis, color.feedback.danger.bg, color.feedback.danger.text, color.feedback.success.bg, color.feedback.success.text, color.feedback.warning.bg, color.feedback.warning.text, color.surface.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.md, font.family.sans, font.weight.semibold, radius.container, radius.pill, size.5, size.6, space.0-5, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.4, typography.ui.line-height, typography.ui.size
- Use it for:
  - What a change needs before it ships: design rules, developer tests, design approval.
  - A short setup the reader goes through once, where each step has a clear done state.
  - Put the action for a row on that row (an Approve button next to Design approval), as a Button with size sm and variant secondary. On narrow screens it takes the full width under the row.
  - Use footer for what the rows add up to: why it waits, and the one way to unblock it.
  - Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use checklistHtml() and checklistRowHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup, status icons and screen reader words, without React.
- Not for:
  - Something the reader ticks off: use Checkbox. A Checklist row shows a status the system knows, it is not a control.
  - A single message about the page: use Alert.
  - A long log of events in time: use a list or a table with dates.
  - Steps the reader moves through one screen at a time: use a stepper or Tabs.
- Accessibility:
  - A list (ul) named by label: "What it needs to ship, list, 3 items".
  - Each row says its status in words before the detail (Done, Failed, Waiting, Needs attention), in visually hidden text. The icon is decorative, so color and shape are never the only signal. Override the words per row with statusLabel.
  - A row's action is a real Button on the row, reached with Tab in reading order, after the row it acts on.
  - Feedback icon colors are checked against their tinted backgrounds in both themes.
  - Static markup: no hydration needed. Plain scripts render the same markup with checklistHtml() and checklistRowHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom.
- Do: Say who or what each row waits on. The detail turns a status into a next step: "Waiting on a design owner" tells the reader whom to ask.
- Do: Name what failed, with numbers. "2 of 212 tests fail" says how bad it is and where to look. "Tests failed" does not.
- Don't: A title without a detail. An icon and a title alone leave the reader guessing what to do. Every row that is not done says why in one line.
- Don't: Warning for something that simply waits. Waiting is normal: use the empty ring. Keep warning for a row that needs attention, such as an approval given before the last change.

### CodeBlock

A command or a short piece of code in IBM Plex Mono, with a copy button on the same line. The button says Copied for two seconds, so the reader knows the paste will work.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.sm, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.mono, font.family.sans, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, radius.control, radius.inset, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, typography.caption.line-height, typography.caption.size, typography.ui.line-height, typography.ui.size
- Use it for:
  - A command the reader runs or pastes: an install line, an MCP server setup, a CLI call.
  - A short snippet the reader copies as is: a CSS variable in use, an import line.
  - Commands wrap, code scrolls (the default): a one-line command breaks at spaces only, never inside a package name or a flag, so the reader sees all of it; code with several lines keeps its layout and scrolls sideways inside the block. Set wrap to choose.
  - hideCopy for code the reader should read, not paste: a file path, an example output.
  - Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use codeBlockHtml() and bindCodeBlocks() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup and the same copy behavior, without React.
- Not for:
  - A token name or value inside a sentence or a table cell: use TokenValue.
  - A whole file or a long diff: link to it, or show it in a dedicated viewer.
  - Inline code in running text: use the code element of the page's prose styles.
- Accessibility:
  - The copy button is a real Button. With a string label it is named Copy plus the label (Copy install); after a copy it reads Copied.
  - A polite live region announces Copied to the clipboard. If the clipboard is blocked, the code is selected and the region says to press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
  - A block that does not wrap is keyboard focusable (tabindex 0), so a long line can be scrolled with the arrow keys. A wrapped block needs no focus stop.
  - Copy works without hydration: statically rendered blocks carry data-code-block hooks and bindCodeBlocks() from @bridge-ds/react/dom wires them. Plain scripts render the same markup with codeBlockHtml().
  - Code text uses color.text.default on color.bg.subtle, checked in both themes.
- Do: Name what the code does. A short label above the block (Install, Add the MCP server) tells the reader which block to copy, and names the copy button for screen readers: Copy install.
- Do: One command per block. Two steps are two blocks, each with its own label and copy button. The reader pastes one thing at a time and sees which one worked.
- Don't: A prompt sign in the code. The block copies exactly what it shows. A leading $ ends up in the terminal and the command fails.
- Don't: Several commands chained in one block. A row of commands joined with && is hard to read and fails as a whole. Split it into one block per step.

### Divider

A hairline that separates groups of content, horizontally or vertically, with an optional short label.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, divider.line, divider.text, font.family.sans, font.size.100, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, size.4, space.2, space.3, space.4
- Use it for:
  - Between groups that belong to the same surface but differ in kind: settings sections, toolbar groups.
  - Labelled, to name what follows ("Older changes") or to offer an alternative ("Or").
- Not for:
  - Between every list item: use spacing, or row borders in a Table.
  - To separate sections that have headings: the heading and space already do it.
- Accessibility:
  - Base UI Separator: role separator with aria-orientation, announced as a boundary.
  - The labelled variant renders two separators around plain text, so the label is read once in order.
  - The line uses border.default (decorative); never rely on it to convey meaning.
- Do: Vertical dividers between toolbar groups. They group related controls without adding boxes.
- Don't: Stacked dividers and borders. A divider next to a card edge doubles the line. Pick one.

### Kbd

Shows a keyboard key or a key combination, as nested kbd elements in the mono face.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.text.muted, font.family.mono, font.family.sans, font.line-height.none, font.size.100, font.weight.medium, kbd.bg, kbd.border, kbd.border-bottom, kbd.radius, kbd.text, size.4, size.5, space.0-5, space.1
- Use it for:
  - Teaching a shortcut in a tooltip, a menu item, an empty state or help text.
  - Inside an Input suffix to hint at the search shortcut.
- Not for:
  - Code or token names: use code.
  - Buttons: a Kbd is not clickable.
- Accessibility:
  - Outer kbd wraps one kbd per key, the HTML pattern for keys pressed together; the plus signs are aria-hidden.
  - Abbreviated keys (Cmd, Esc, arrows) carry a title with the full name.
  - Text color is text.muted on surface (4.5:1).
- Do: Write the platform's key names. Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere. Abbreviations get a title with the full name.
- Don't: Long sequences. More than three keys is a recipe, not a shortcut. Explain it in text.

### Table

A semantic data table for comparing records: sortable columns, selectable rows, density-aware rows, and a focusable scroll region on narrow screens.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, card.border, color.border.default, color.signal.default, color.surface.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, control.height.md, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.offset, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.line-height.snug, font.size.100, font.size.200, font.size.300, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, font.weight.semibold, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, radius.container, radius.inset, size.6, space.1, space.2, space.3, space.8, table.border, table.cell-padding-x, table.header.bg, table.header.text, table.row-height, table.row.bg-hover, table.row.bg-selected
- Use it for:
  - Records with the same attributes that users compare, sort or act on: tokens, components, pull requests.
  - Sortable headers (sortDirection + onSort, or useTableSort) on columns users reorder by.
  - Selectable rows: a Checkbox in the first cell, selected on the row, bulk actions above the table.
  - Compact density for expert, data-heavy screens.
  - Column widths when one column should not take the space of the others: width on the header cell, as a token length (var(--size-20)), a percentage or a fraction (0.35), plus minWidth for a floor. layout fixed keeps them exact while data loads.
  - narrowLayout stack when people read the table on a phone: under about 480px each row becomes a card, every value beside its column name. Keep scroll (the default) for wide data people compare across rows.
- Not for:
  - Layout: never use a table to position content.
  - Fewer than three attributes per item: use a list.
  - Editing many cells inline like a spreadsheet: that needs a grid pattern, not in the system yet.
- Accessibility:
  - Native table, thead, th scope col and td: screen readers announce headers with each cell.
  - Sortable headers contain a button; the th gets aria-sort ascending or descending on the sorted column only.
  - Selected rows set aria-selected and use the selected surface plus a checked Checkbox (never color alone).
  - The scroll container is a labelled region with tabIndex 0, so keyboard users can scroll wide tables (named by the caption or aria-label).
  - Row height and cell padding follow density: 48/36px rows, both above the 24px target minimum for the controls inside.
  - Stacked rows keep their table roles (table, row, cell), so screen readers still read cell by cell; the column names shown before each value are the header texts. The header row is hidden while rows stack, so put sorting somewhere else on phones.
- Do: Right-align numbers. numeric aligns digits on the right with tabular figures, so values compare at a glance.
- Do: Say what to do when it is empty. TableEmpty keeps the header in place and explains how rows will appear.
- Don't: Color as the only row state. A tinted row alone does not say selected. Pair it with a checked Checkbox.

### Tag

A compact label for a value. Static to describe, toggleable as a filter chip, or removable to show selected values.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.action.disabled.bg, color.action.disabled.text, color.surface.pressed, color.text.default, focus.ring.color, focus.ring.width, font.family.sans, font.line-height.tight, font.size.100, font.tracking.wide, font.weight.medium, motion.duration.instant, motion.easing.standard, size.5, size.6, space.0-5, space.1, space.2, tag.bg, tag.bg-hover, tag.bg-selected, tag.border, tag.radius, tag.signal-bg, tag.signal-text, tag.text, tag.text-selected
- Use it for:
  - Filter chips above a table or a list: toggle tags in a labelled group.
  - Selected values in a multi-select Combobox or a filter bar: removable tags.
  - Static metadata: token groups, platforms, component categories.
- Not for:
  - Status (Published, Failed): use Badge.
  - Actions: use Button. A tag describes a value; it does not do something.
  - Choosing one option out of several: use RadioGroup or Tabs.
- Accessibility:
  - Toggle tags are Base UI Toggle buttons with aria-pressed; selected also shows a check icon, so selection is not color alone.
  - The remove button is a separate button named "Remove <label>" (removeLabel when the text is not a plain string).
  - Both buttons have the focus ring and are reachable with Tab; Enter and Space activate them.
  - Static tags are plain text with no role.
- Do: Put filter chips in a named group. role group with aria-label ("Filter by theme") tells screen reader users what the chips control.
- Don't: Sentences in tags. Tags truncate. Keep them to a value of one to three words.

### TokenValue

A token name and its value in IBM Plex Mono, with a color swatch when the value is a color. For token tables, before and after values, and the values behind a conflict choice.

- Family: Data display
- Tokens: border-width.default, color.bg.subtle, color.border.default, color.border.emphasis, color.surface.default, color.text.default, color.text.muted, font.family.mono, icon.size.sm, icon.size.xs, radius.inset, radius.xs, space.0-5, space.1-5, typography.caption.line-height, typography.caption.size, typography.ui.line-height, typography.ui.size
- Use it for:
  - Showing a token in a table, a review or a change list: the name, the value as written, and the resolved value when it is an alias.
  - Before and after a change: the previous value with previous (struck through), then the new value.
  - Inside a ChoiceCard description, so the reader sees the value each choice keeps.
  - size sm in dense tables and inside sentences; md everywhere else.
  - Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use tokenValueHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup and swatch rules, without React.
- Not for:
  - A command or a snippet the reader copies: use CodeBlock.
  - A status such as Changed or Removed: use Badge next to the value.
  - Editing a value: use an Input, and show the TokenValue as the current value next to it.
- Accessibility:
  - Static text, no interaction: screen readers read the name, the value and the resolved value in order.
  - The swatch is decorative (aria-hidden): the value text always says the color, so the swatch is never the only signal.
  - A previous value is wrapped in del, so assistive technology that reports deletions reads it as removed, and it is struck through for sighted readers.
  - The swatch carries a hairline border, so white and near-background colors still read as a square in both themes.
  - Long names and aliases break anywhere instead of overflowing a narrow cell.
  - Plain scripts render the same markup with tokenValueHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom.
- Do: Show the alias and what it resolves to. The alias says where the value comes from, the resolved value says what the reader will see. Together they answer both questions in one glance.
- Do: Pair a previous value with the new one. The struck-through value reads as removed, the plain one as the new value. Keep them on one line, old first.
- Don't: Repeating the token name in its own row. When the row or column already names the token, drop name and show the value only. The same name twice is noise.
- Don't: A previous value on its own. A struck-through value without the new one tells the reader what is gone but not what replaces it.

### Container

Centers page content at a max width from the size scale with token side padding. Phones always get a 16px gutter.

- Family: Layout
- Tokens: size.160, size.180, size.240, size.300, space.4, space.6, space.8
- Use it for:
  - The outer wrapper of a page or a page section.
  - sm for forms and reading (keeps lines under about 75 characters), lg for settings, xl for dashboards and tables.
  - render={<main />} on the page's main region.
- Not for:
  - Inside cards or dialogs: they already set their width and padding.
  - Full-bleed backgrounds: put the background on an outer element and the Container inside it.
- Accessibility:
  - A plain div by default; render as <main /> for the main region so the landmark exists.
  - Content reflows at 320px wide without horizontal scroll (WCAG 1.4.10).
- Do: Match the width to the content. Forms in an xl container stretch inputs to unreadable lengths. Pick sm.
- Don't: Nested containers. A container inside a container doubles the padding and adds nothing.

### Grid

Two-dimensional layout with token gaps: a fixed number of equal columns, or as many columns as fit for card and tile grids.

- Family: Layout
- Tokens: layout.gap
- Use it for:
  - Card and tile grids: minItemWidth makes them responsive without breakpoints.
  - Dashboards and settings layouts with a fixed column count.
  - render={<ul />} when the cells are a list of items.
- Not for:
  - Tabular data with headers: use Table.
  - A single row or column: use Inline or Stack.
- Accessibility:
  - A plain div by default with no role; it is not a data grid. Use Table for data.
  - Cells flow in DOM order, so reading and tab order follow the visual order row by row.
- Do: Prefer minItemWidth for tiles. Tiles reflow from four columns to one as space shrinks, with no media queries.
- Don't: Many fixed columns on small screens. Twelve fixed columns at phone width make unreadable slivers. Use minItemWidth or fewer columns.

### Inline

Lays out children in a row with a token gap and wraps them when space runs out: badges, button rows, metadata.

- Family: Layout
- Tokens: space.2
- Use it for:
  - Rows of related small items: badges, tags, buttons, meta text.
  - justify="between" for page and card headers: title at the start, actions at the end.
  - wrap={false} only when the row must stay on one line and can scroll or truncate.
- Not for:
  - A vertical list: use Stack.
  - Columns that must line up across rows: use Grid or Table.
- Accessibility:
  - A plain div by default; use render for a list (<ul />) when the items are a list.
  - Wrapping never reorders items, so the visual and tab order match.
- Do: Let rows wrap. Wrapping keeps every item reachable at narrow widths and at 200% zoom.
- Don't: Fixed widths inside an Inline. Fixed widths fight the wrap and overflow on phones. Let content size the items.

### PageHeader

The top of a page: the page title, a one-line lead that says what the page is for, an optional meta line (freshness, counts) and up to three page actions.

- Family: Layout
- Tokens: color.text.default, color.text.muted, font.family.sans, font.line-height.normal, font.size.100, font.tracking.wide, size.120, size.8, space.2, space.3, space.4, space.6, space.8, typography.body.line-height, typography.body.size, typography.h1.line-height, typography.h1.size, typography.h1.tracking, typography.h1.weight, typography.h2.family, typography.h2.line-height, typography.h2.size, typography.h2.tracking, typography.h2.weight, typography.h3.family, typography.h3.line-height, typography.h3.size, typography.h3.tracking, typography.h3.weight
- Use it for:
  - Once at the top of every page, so titles, leads and actions sit in the same place across the product.
  - lead: one or two sentences on what the page is for, not how to use it.
  - meta: a quiet line for facts that build trust, like when the page was last updated or where its data comes from.
  - actions: the page-level actions (Edit in Studio, Create token). Keep the primary one last.
  - headingLevel 2 when the header tops a section inside a page that already has an h1.
- Not for:
  - Section titles inside a page: use a plain h2 heading.
  - Dialogs and drawers: they have their own title slot.
  - Promotional heroes with art and several calls to action: build them in the page, outside the system.
- Accessibility:
  - Renders a header element with a real heading (h1 by default), so the page outline and screen reader heading navigation start here.
  - One h1 per page: use headingLevel 2 when the page already has one.
  - Actions keep their own roles: a Button for actions on this page, a link (Button with render={<a />}) for navigation.
  - The meta line is plain text in the muted color, which passes AA on every surface.
- Do: Name the page as the navigation does. The title repeats the sidebar label, so users know they landed where they clicked.
- Do: Keep the lead to one idea. One or two sentences that say what the page is for. Details belong in the content.
- Don't: A paragraph as the lead. A long lead pushes the content below the fold and nobody reads it.
- Don't: Title in all caps or title case. Sentence case reads faster and matches the rest of the interface.

### Stack

Stacks children in a column with a gap from the space scale. The default gap follows density (16px comfortable, 12px compact).

- Family: Layout
- Tokens: layout.gap
- Use it for:
  - Vertical rhythm inside cards, dialogs, forms and page sections.
  - gap from the space scale: tight (1 to 2) inside a group, generous (6 to 8) between groups.
  - render to output a semantic element: <section />, <ul />, <form />.
- Not for:
  - Rows of items: use Inline.
  - Two-dimensional layouts with columns: use Grid.
  - Spacing one element only: give that element a margin class in your app, not a wrapper.
- Accessibility:
  - A plain div by default with no role: it changes layout, not semantics.
  - Use render to give the stack the right element (a list of items should be <ul />).
  - Visual order equals DOM order, so reading and tab order stay consistent.
- Do: Nest stacks to show grouping. A tight stack per group inside a looser stack: the space itself says what belongs together.
- Don't: One gap for everything. Equal spacing everywhere flattens hierarchy. Vary the gap to separate groups.
